rationale: While the initial discovery cohort (Fliedner et al., 2020) and subsequent single case reports described intellectual disability as a universal or defining feature across evaluated patients, the largest multi-center cohort to date (Schmid et al., 2025, evaluating 50 novel individuals) conclusively shows that cognitive ability is variable and exhibits incomplete penetrance, ranging from strictly normal IQ to severe intellectual disability, with the majority falling in the borderline to mild ID range.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 50 novel individuals harboring SCAF4 variants, cognitive abilities were documented to range from normal IQ to severe intellectual disability, with borderline to mild ID in the majority, demonstrating that intellectual disability is not an obligatory phenotype.

source.title: Further delineation of the SCAF4-associated neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: Cognitive abilities ranged from normal IQ to severe intellectual disability (ID), with borderline to mild ID in the majority of individuals.

evidence.text: The initial discovery study identified nine likely pathogenic germline variants where all affected individuals presented with mild intellectual disability, seizures, behavioral abnormalities, and structural anomalies, establishing the initial assumption of complete penetrance for neurodevelopmental impairment.

source.title: Variants in SCAF4 cause a neurodevelopmental disorder and are associated with impaired mRNA processing
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Affected individuals demonstrated a variable neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by mild intellectual disability, seizures, behavioral abnormalities, and various skeletal and structural anomalies.

evidence.text: A 16-year-old male with a de novo truncating frameshift variant in SCAF4 presented with syndromic intellectual disability, severe speech impairment, epilepsy, and structural malformations, aligning with the more severe end of the cognitive spectrum.

source.title: SCAF4‐related syndromic intellectual disability
source.journal: American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A
source.quote: We performed exome sequencing in a 16-year-old Brazilian male presenting with ID, epilepsy, behavioral problems, speech impairment, facial dysmorphisms, heart malformations, and obesity.

evidence.text: Identification of SCAF4 variants in three individuals presenting primarily with focal epilepsy showed associated intellectual disability or motor retardation alongside skeletal abnormalities.

source.title: SCAF4 variants associated with focal epilepsy accompanied by multisystem disorders
source.quote: All patients had focal seizures and focal discharges on EEG recordings, with intellectual disability or motor retardation, skeletal abnormalities, and one had cryptorchidism.

evidence.text: A 4-year and 7-month-old boy with a paternally inherited nonsense SCAF4 mutation displayed intellectual impairment and language development delay.

source.title: A novel nonsense mutation in SCAF4 associated with fliedner-zweier syndrome: a case report and literature review
source.quote: We present the case of a 4-year and seven-month-old Chinese boy displaying intellectual impairment, language development disorder, behavioral abnormalities, and distinct facial features.

conflicts: Earlier discovery cohorts and smaller case studies reported intellectual disability in 100% of affected individuals due to ascertainment bias (testing only patients selected for neurodevelopmental delay/ID), whereas broader cohort matching in 50 patients established that cognitive penetrance is incomplete, including patients with normal IQ.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of transmitting parents who carry pathogenic SCAF4 variants have normal cognitive function versus unrecognized borderline intellectual disability?
new_directions.rationale: Thirteen of the 50 variants in Schmid et al. and the variant in PMC12021868 were inherited; comprehensive standardized neuropsychological assessment of carrier parents is critical to determine the exact non-penetrance rate of cognitive impairment.

new_directions.question_text: Do C-terminal truncating or specific CTD-interacting domain missense variants correlate with normal IQ, indicating an intragenic genotype-phenotype gradient?
new_directions.rationale: Schmid et al. noted that variants in the CTD-interacting domain and C-terminal region have differing predicted structural impacts compared to classic N-terminal early-truncating loss-of-function variants.
